Heron Power, an American power electronics manufacturer, announced the selection of Morgan Hill, California, as the site of its first large-scale factory. Heron Power evaluated several locations across multiple states before selecting Morgan Hill, a site close to its engineering headquarters and the broader Bay Area's technology and manufacturing talent pool. The City of Morgan Hill, utility PG&E, and California state partners worked with Heron Power and its real estate advisor JLL for ten months to finalize the site selection. The factory, named Heron Factory One, is designed to produce up to 10,000 Heron Link units per year, according to the company. This 5-megawatt medium voltage power conversion system is intended for large-scale energy projects and data centers. Heron will convert the former 286,000 sq ft (26,570 sqm) distribution warehouse, just south of San Jose, into a manufacturing facility to produce its 5MW Heron Link medium-voltage power conversion system, targeted for data center and large-scale energy projects. hits.title: Heatmap News: America’s Transformer Crisis Has Supercharged a Wave of New Startups | Heron Power
hits.snippet: “It does what a traditional transformer does, but it also does what switchgear does, what tap changers do, what capacitor banks do, and what a synchronous condenser does, in a single package, managed in real time by software,” Heron’s CEO Drew Baglino told me via email. During Baglino’s prior tenure leading the development and deployment of Tesla's EV Superchargers and large-scale battery storage systems, he constantly found conventional transformers to be “a supply chain constraint, a deployment bottleneck, and a physical hazard,” leading him to believe there simply had to be a better way. But because solid-state designs are driven by software-controlled power electronics rather than fixed hardware, that fundamentally shifts the paradigm, he said. “A traditional transformer that's wrong for the job gets ripped out and replaced.
